## Introduction

<div style="text-align: center;">
  <img src="./img/dropseq_logo.png" alt="Dropseq Logo" width="200px"/>
  <img src="./img/nextflow_logo.png" alt="Nextflow Logo" width="100px"/>
</div>

This vignette demonstrates how to run the nf-core/scalpel pipeline on a Drop-seq dataset from the study of [Franz Ake et al](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-61118-0) on human neuronal differentiation.

The full dataset is publicly available on GEO at accession [GSE268222](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE268222).

SCALPEL requires as input for each sample the FASTQ files, the BAM file and the gene expression (DGE) count matrix generated by Drop-seq tools. For the purpose of this demonstration, we provide a subset of the original data: [reduced_GSE268222](https://zenodo.org/records/17176865/files/reduced_GSE268222.tar.gz?download=1).

```{sh}
> wget -O reduced_GSE268222.tar.gz https://zenodo.org/records/17176865/files/reduced_GSE268222.tar.gz?download=1
> tar -xvf reduced_GSE268222.tar.gz
> tree -L 2 reduced_GSE268222
reduced_GSE268222
├── dropseq_files
│   ├── hiPSCs.bam
│   ├── hiPSCs.counts.txt
│   ├── NPCs.bam
│   └── NPCs.counts.txt
├── fastq_files
│   ├── hiPSCs_1000000_lib_16058AAB_CTCTCTAC_read1_001.fastq.gz
│   ├── hiPSCs_1000000_lib_16058AAB_CTCTCTAC_read2_001.fastq.gz
│   ├── NPCs_1000000_lib_16057AAB_TAGGCATG_read1_001.fastq.gz
│   └── NPCs_1000000_lib_16057AAB_TAGGCATG_read2_001.fastq.gz
├── hiPSCs_barcodes.txt
└── NPCs_barcodes.txt

3 directories, 10 files
```

SCALPEL requires a **GTF genome annotation** and a **FASTA transcript annotation** of your organism, and the **genome FASTA** (used to build the internal priming reference). For the current analysis, we use a reduced annotation reference from GENCODE for Human (GENCODE.v41).

- [reduced_GENCODE.v41.annotation.gtf](https://zenodo.org/records/17176838/files/reduced_GENCODE.v41.annotation.gtf.gz?download=1)
- [GENCODE.v41.transcript.fa](https://ftp.ebi.ac.uk/pub/databases/gencode/Gencode_human/release_41/gencode.v41.transcripts.fa.gz)
- [hg38 genome (UCSC)](https://hgdownload.soe.ucsc.edu/goldenPath/hg38/bigZips/hg38.fa.gz)

```{sh}
> wget -O reduced_GENCODE.v41.annotation.gtf.gz https://zenodo.org/records/17176838/files/reduced_GENCODE.v41.annotation.gtf.gz?download=1
> wget https://ftp.ebi.ac.uk/pub/databases/gencode/Gencode_human/release_41/gencode.v41.transcripts.fa.gz
> wget https://hgdownload.soe.ucsc.edu/goldenPath/hg38/bigZips/hg38.fa.gz
```

Complete GTF genome annotation and FASTA transcripts annotation can be downloaded from [GENCODE](https://www.gencodegenes.org) or [ENSEMBL](https://www.ensembl.org/info/data/ftp/index.html).

## SCALPEL running

### Samplesheet

To run SCALPEL, you must provide a **samplesheet.csv** file (`--samplesheet`), with a header and one row per sample:

1. **sample**: sample name (no spaces).
2. **fastq_1**: R1 FASTQ file.
3. **fastq_2**: R2 FASTQ file.
4. **cranger_path**: BAM file of the sample (Drop-seq tools, with `XC` cell barcode and `XM` UMI tags; an index is created if missing).
5. **dge**: DGE count matrix of the sample (Drop-seq tools, `.txt` or `.txt.gz`).

Paths can be absolute or relative to the samplesheet directory. A sample sequenced in several runs is given as several rows with the same sample name.

```{sh}
> cat samplesheet.csv
sample,fastq_1,fastq_2,cranger_path,dge
hiPSCs,reduced_GSE268222/fastq_files/hiPSCs_1000000_lib_16058AAB_CTCTCTAC_read1_001.fastq.gz,reduced_GSE268222/fastq_files/hiPSCs_1000000_lib_16058AAB_CTCTCTAC_read2_001.fastq.gz,reduced_GSE268222/dropseq_files/hiPSCs.bam,reduced_GSE268222/dropseq_files/hiPSCs.counts.txt
NPCs,reduced_GSE268222/fastq_files/NPCs_1000000_lib_16057AAB_TAGGCATG_read1_001.fastq.gz,reduced_GSE268222/fastq_files/NPCs_1000000_lib_16057AAB_TAGGCATG_read2_001.fastq.gz,reduced_GSE268222/dropseq_files/NPCs.bam,reduced_GSE268222/dropseq_files/NPCs.counts.txt
```

### Execution

To execute SCALPEL, use the following command:

```{sh}
nextflow run plasslab/nf-core-scalpel -r dev \
    -profile conda \
    --sequencing_platform dropseq \
    --samplesheet samplesheet.csv \
    --transcriptome gencode.v41.transcripts.fa.gz \
    --gtf reduced_GENCODE.v41.annotation.gtf.gz \
    --genome hg38.fa.gz \
    --outdir results
```

### Options

#### Cell barcodes

You can restrict the analysis to selected cells with a **barcodes_whitelist.csv** file (`--barcodes_whitelist`) giving the barcode file of each sample (one barcode per line, as in the BAM `XC` tag). For example, with the 100 barcodes per sample provided in the `reduced_GSE268222` directory:

```{sh}
> cat barcodes_whitelist.csv
sample,barcodes
hiPSCs,reduced_GSE268222/hiPSCs_barcodes.txt
NPCs,reduced_GSE268222/NPCs_barcodes.txt
```

and add `--barcodes_whitelist barcodes_whitelist.csv` to the command.

#### Cell clusters

To compare cell clusters instead of samples in the differential isoform usage, provide a `--clusters` file (`sample,barcode,cluster`).

#### Pre-built internal priming reference

The internal priming reference built from `--genome` is saved to `<outdir>/ip_reference/`. It can be reused, or replaced by the provided [GRCh38 reference](https://zenodo.org/records/15717592/files/hg38_ipriming_sites.bed.tar.gz?download=1), with `--ip_reference` (`--genome` is then not needed):

```{sh}
    --ip_reference hg38_ipriming_sites.bed.tar.gz
```

The generation from the genome works for any assembly or species (e.g. T2T).

#### Profiles and resources

Use `-profile docker`, `singularity` or `apptainer` instead of `conda` (add `emulate_amd64` on Apple Silicon with Docker), and `-resume` to restart a run from its completed steps.

::: {.callout-tip}
The salmon steps request 36 GB of memory by default. On a laptop or a small server, cap the resources with a config file given with `-c local.config`:

```{sh}
> cat local.config
process {
    resourceLimits = [cpus: 8, memory: '14.GB', time: '6.h']
}
```
:::

::: {.callout-warning}
The BAM files, the GTF annotation and the internal priming reference must use the same chromosome names (e.g. 'chr1', ..., 'chrM' vs '1', ..., 'MT'). The pipeline checks this before processing the reads and stops with an explicit message in case of mismatch. Use references from the same source as the BAM files.
:::

### Main parameters

| Parameter            | Default | Description                                                                |
| -------------------- | ------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--distance_3end`    | `100`   | Maximum distance (nt) between the 3' ends of collapsed isoforms.           |
| `--distance_profile` | `500`   | Window (nt from the 3' end) where collapsed isoforms have identical exons. |
| `--distance_reads`   | `600`   | Maximum distance (nt) of a read from the isoform 3' end.                   |
| `--min_mapq`         | `255`   | Minimum mapping quality (255: uniquely mapped reads).                      |
| `--distance_ip`      | `200`   | Internal priming sites closer to the 3' end are ignored.                   |
| `--gene_fraction`    | `98%`   | Genes used to learn the read distance distribution.                        |
| `--binsize`          | `20`    | Bin size (nt) of the read distance distribution.                           |

See the [usage documentation](https://github.com/plasslab/nf-core-scalpel/blob/dev/docs/usage.md) for all options.

Following the successful execution of SCALPEL, the output directory (`results`) contains:

- **differential/iDGE_seurat.RDS**:\
The Seurat object containing the isoform expression data (iDGE) of all samples (one counts layer per sample, cells named `<sample>_<barcode>`). This object can be used for downstream analysis and visualization in R.

- **differential/DIU_table.csv**:\
A table summarizing the differential isoform usage (DIU) events between the samples (or the clusters given with `--clusters`).

- **dge/sampleXXX_iDGE/**:\
The isoform count matrix (iDGE) of each sample, in sparse 10x format (`matrix.mtx.gz`, `features.tsv.gz` with `gene***isoform` features, `barcodes.tsv.gz`), readable with `Seurat::Read10X()`.

- **filtered_bams/sampleXXX_filtered.bam(.bai)**:\
The reads used for the quantification (duplicated reads and internal priming associated reads discarded, only reads passing the SCALPEL filters).

- **isoform/**:\
The selected isoforms, reusable with `--isoform_annotation` to quantify new samples on the same isoforms.

- **ip_reference/**:\
The internal priming reference built from the genome (reusable with `--ip_reference`).

- **probability/**:\
The read distance distribution to the 3' end of each sample.

- **pipeline_info/**:\
Execution reports and software versions.

The other directories contain intermediate files of each step (see the [output documentation](https://github.com/plasslab/nf-core-scalpel/blob/dev/docs/output.md)).

## Downstream analysis

For more information, refer to [SCALPEL_downstream_analysis](https://raw.githack.com/plasslab/nf-core-scalpel/refs/heads/dev/docs/vignettes/dropseq_downstream.html) for downstream analysis of the SCALPEL output files.
